messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ⛑️ detected: elevated routing fallback rates from eu-west -> us-central; fallback model 'small-lm-v2' rising to 32% (threshold 5%). Paging oncall.

sara: Oncall sara here. Confirming — dashboards show a spike starting ~08:12 UTC, sustained. Latency for affected requests up ~450ms and error rate +2.5% for platinum tier. Looks like spillover from eu-west into us-central pool.

jamal: grabbing logs now. Can someone paste the routing decision traces for a sample req-id? Need decision path: prefer_region / fallback list / tier policy.

sara: here's a short extract of the routing trace for req-id 7f3a2b:
```text
2025-09-14T08:12:13Z req=7f3a2b tier=platinum src_region=eu-west target_route=eu-west:model_base
decision: region_unavailable -> apply_fallbacks
fallback_candidates=[eu-west:model_small_quant, us-central:model_base, us-central:model_small]
selected=us-central:model_small (fallback_index=2)
latency=482ms error=null
```

jamal: hmm we expected eu-west:model_small_quant to be preferred before crossing region. @eng-runtime can you pull the policy config for platinum routing precedence? maybe policy mismatch after last deploy.

eng-runtime: I see a policy drift. The consolidated routing config we shipped in last deploy accidentally reordered fallback_candidates when prefer_same_region=false. The intended order for platinum was: same-region variants (base, quant), then cross-region base. But the effective comparator used model size first -> so small variants got prioritized even if cross-region would be lower-latency. Looks like a comparator bug: comparator prioritized model_size over region_priority for premium tiers.

ops-rotations: Customer impact summary from SLOs: 5 paying customers saw degraded p99s and a handful of 5xx retries. No data leakage. We flagged 3 active sessions that hit timeouts and retried to different model variants, increasing token costs. CS notified.

customer-success-bot: Notified customers: acme-inc, neptune-analytics, clearcast. Escalation opened: CS-2379. Slack thread created in #customer-ops.

sara: Hypothesis list (H1/H2) — please add/check:
H1: comparator ordering bug in routing config after recent config merge -> wrong fallback ordering -> cross-region small model chosen.
H2: transient eu-west capacity evictions causing region_unavailable signals -> valid spillover but wrong candidate order worsened perf.
H3: cache/KV-miss amplification making small model selection more common (hot prefix issues).

maria: I'll track hypotheses. Assigning owners:
H1 -> @eng-runtime (investigate comparator + deploy diff)
H2 -> @sara (capacity and node evictions)
H3 -> @jamal (KV/cache correlation)

jamal: logs for correlation ids attached (paste):
```log
req=7f3a2b event=route_decide comparator_order=[model_size, region_priority, pool_health]
req=8c44f01 event=eviction node=eu-west-3 reason=OOM timestamp=2025-09-14T08:11:55Z
req=a9f22c event=kv_miss prefix=customer:acme session=xyz
```

eng-runtime: Confirmed comparator bug. The comparator unit tests didn't cover tier override semantics; a recent refactor compacted comparator keys and inadvertently changed stable sort guarantees. Reproduced locally with unit test; patch ready.

sara: Immediate mitigation: can we temporarily flip fallback_order for 'platinum' to prefer same-region base variants? That's quick and low-risk.

eng-runtime: Running a rolling policy update now (no deploy). Command:
```bash
redwoodctl routing update --tier platinum --set fallback_order="[same_region_base,same_region_quant,cross_region_base]" --reason "emergency: routing misorder"
```

incident-bot: ACTION: routing update initiated by eng-runtime at 2025-09-14T08:28:10Z; policy change id=policy-1224; targeting eu-west and global control-plane.

ops-rotations: Observability after change — fallback rate dropped from 32% -> 6% within 2 minutes, latency p99 trending back down. No further customer 5xx reports after 08:30 UTC.

leo: leo taking next shift (08:40 UTC handoff). Summary for next oncall: comparator bug caused wrong fallback ordering -> chose 'small' across regions -> higher latency & retries for platinum. Mitigation: rollback ordering changed via redwoodctl; patch to comparator in PR#8456 by eng-runtime. Please add post-incident tests.

maria: I'll author RCA skeleton and hypothesis timeline. Timeline notes:
- 08:11:55Z node eviction eu-west-3 (possible trigger)
- 08:12:13Z first observed high fallback rate & misroutes (req samples)
- 08:18:30Z routing rate climbs past threshold
- 08:28:10Z policy update (fallback_order) executed
- 08:30:20Z metrics recover

sara: Follow-ups we should list in RCA:
- enforce comparator ordering tests (unit + integration)
- add canary checks for routing config changes (simulate tier-specific fallbacks)
- telemetry: record comparator decision key ordering in traces for quick forensics
- run a model-candidate stress test to simulate region evictions

jamal: added log snippets and correlation IDs into the RCA doc draft (PR linked in #eng-releases). Also recommend a guard: if cross-region fallback would increase latency by >200ms, prefer falling back to a less-loaded same-region small model instead of jumping region.

eng-runtime: PR#8456 contains the comparator fix + added test cases and a canary step in redwoodctl. I'll own postmortem and follow-up ticket list.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED ✅: fallback rates normalized and customer impact contained. Recorded incident id = INC-20250914-17. Please close after RCA publish.

leo: Thanks team. I'll make sure owners get follow-up tasks into sprint board and assign CS postmortem notes. Good handoff. :thumbsup:

maria: I'll post the draft RCA in #incidents by EOD and request reviews from eng-runtime, jamal, and sara. Closing notes: root cause = comparator ordering bug combined with transient eu-west node evictions that amplified spillover. Preventative controls listed above.

sara: Closing thread from oncall — feel free to ping me if any follow-ups needed. Nice work everyone. :tada:
